models.description: OpenAI GPT Image 2.5 Sunburst: text-to-image generation and editing of up to 16 reference images with an optional mask.

families.notes: One schema for all five ids, apart from descriptions. Sending `image` switches Router from generation to the edit operation, and the body leaves it out when no image is connected. `image` takes a data URI or a signed Comfy-asset https URL. data URIs are used because arbitrary https hosts are refused. Only png, webp and jpeg are accepted, with at most 25 MiB per image and 64 MiB per request. `mask` must be a PNG with an alpha channel, under 4 MiB, the same size as the first image. Router removes it when there is no image. `output_format` is fixed to png and `output_compression` is hidden, because the result reader cannot map the response's `output_format` ('png') to a mime type. The OpenAI-served response is always inline `data[].b64_json`. The fal, Runware or WaveSpeed fallback for gpt-image-2 returns `data[].url` only, hence the second media path. Exposed params: size (free string, e.g. 1024x1024, 1536x1024, 1024x1536, auto), quality, background (transparent/opaque), moderation (auto/low). The shared `quality` enum lists low, medium, high, xhigh, max, standard, hd and auto. standard and hd are DALL-E values, and xhigh/max are probably only valid on the 2.x ids, so the app should offer low, medium, high and auto by default. Which ids accept xhigh/max is not stated in the schema. gpt-image-1 sizes are limited to the three fixed sizes plus auto. The schema does not constrain this. The call is sync/direct-return with no queue handle.

families.notes: All 16 recraft/* schemas share one request/response shape (RecraftImageGenerationFields; only prompt required; no additionalProperties restriction). Text-only: Recraft on the Router has no image input (edit/remix/vectorize/upscale are not Router models). Router writes `model` from the path, so it is excluded. Exposed params: size (free string in the schema, e.g. "1024x1024"; the hand-written catalog's enum is a fine UI default), style (free string; Recraft values like realistic_image / digital_illustration / vector_illustration, mainly meaningful for V2/V3), style_id (mutually exclusive with style), plus controls.artistic_level (0-5) and controls.no_text. controls.colors / background_color (RGB arrays) are not exposed. Direct-return, no poll. The *_vector models return an SVG at data[0].url — the app should treat that output as image/svg+xml (the b64 fallback mime image/png is wrong for them, but response_format is fixed to url so it should not be hit). Styles models: see reason; binding is otherwise identical and would work with a user-supplied style_id.

families.notes: Request schema is allOf[$ref IdeogramV3Fields, not(any reference-image field)] — the interpreter must resolve allOf/$ref at params.at "" to find the properties. rendering_speed is REQUIRED (enum DEFAULT|TURBO|QUALITY, schema default DEFAULT): the param must always carry a value (default DEFAULT) or the call fails validation. Exposed params: rendering_speed, aspect_ratio ("WxH" e.g. 1x1, 16x9), resolution ("WxH" e.g. 1280x800), magic_prompt (AUTO|ON|OFF), style_type (AUTO|GENERAL|REALISTIC|DESIGN|FICTION), seed. Ideogram treats aspect_ratio and resolution as alternatives — send one. Style/character reference images are refused by the Router (multipart-only on v1), so no image input. Direct-return. Output URLs are Ideogram's own and expire; an element with no url is a moderated/empty result, hence data[*].url (first match).

families.notes: Exactly one of text_prompt / json_prompt; the app sends text_prompt. Exposed params: rendering_speed (DEFAULT|TURBO|QUALITY, optional here) and resolution (optional WxH; the schema lists the supported 2K values: 2048x2048, 1440x2880, 2880x1440, 1664x2496, 2496x1664, 1792x2240, 2240x1792, 1440x2560, 2560x1440, 1600x2560, 2560x1600, 1728x2304, 2304x1728, 1296x3168, 3168x1296, 1152x2944, 2944x1152, 1248x3328, 3328x1248, 1280x3072, 3072x1280 — omit to let the model choose). enable_copyright_detection left off. No image inputs. Direct-return. Matches the existing hand-verified ideogramV4 mapper.

families.notes: Binds the generate operation: no images is text-to-image; `images` (https URL or data URI, png/webp/jpeg, up to 5, or 4 with a mask) edits, the first being the primary source. The mask is black where Ideogram edits and white where it preserves, matching images[0]'s size; `size` must be omitted with a mask (left empty by default, so it is). Precise Edit (`image` plus `reference_images`) is a separate operation selected by the presence of `image` and is not exposed. quality: very_low is refused without source images. magic_prompt is a free string; paramOverrides gives its documented values. size is free: auto, source or WIDTHxHEIGHT. Direct-return; data[*].url (first match), as for Ideogram 4.0.

families.notes: All four krea/* schemas are identical. Required: prompt, aspect_ratio, resolution. resolution's only enum value is "1K" so it is a literal. aspect_ratio is REQUIRED with no schema default (enum 1:1, 4:3, 3:2, 16:9, 2.35:1, 4:5, 2:3, 9:16): the param must always carry a value — default it to 1:1 in the UI. Other params: creativity (raw|low|medium|high, default medium), seed (nullable number). Image handle maps to image_style_references (max 10, {url, strength}); strength is required by KreaImageStyleReference (range -2..2) and fixed at 1 here — these are style guides, not edit sources, so 'image-to-image' is loose. moodboards (uuid ids) and styles (LoRA ids) not exposed. Router polls Krea itself; a 200 is always status=completed with result.urls non-empty, so the error rule is belt-and-braces.

All five Veo 3.x schemas are byte-identical; per-model limits are NOT in the schema: durationSeconds is a free number (Veo 3/3.1 accept 4, 6, 8), resolution enum lists 4k but only veo-3.1-generate-001 is known to do 4k (fast/lite/3.0: 720p/1080p). models.name: FlashVSR

Output elements are always URLs (no base64 option). `data.error` is "" on success.
